ledger.note: 1441: 'the Xiu plotted revenge and in 1441 revolted against the Cocom' at Mayapan; the Xiu, who 'gradually lost control of Mayapan ... by 1300' and were partly expelled 'in c. 1400', hold Maní afterwards (infobox 'Kuchkabals of Yucatan after 1461').

ledger.note: About 1539: 'The first ambassadors from the Xiu met with Spanish conquistador Francisco de Montejo the Younger at Tuchi-caan, around 1539'; the conquest page says 'the Xiu Maya of Maní allied themselves with the Spanish'. Entered as a tributary alliance; the pages give no tribute.

wars.name: Xiu revolt against Mayapan
wars.outcome: 'In 1441, Ah Xiu Xupan of the powerful noble family of Xiu' revolted and 'all of the Cocom family, except one ... were killed' (Mayapan page); the Xiu page: 'in 1441 revolted against the Cocom'.
wars.note: No land change is dated beyond the fall of Mayapan.

certainty.note: No frontier is recorded; the Mani Land Treaty of 1557 settled the border with Sotuta and Cupul only after this state's end.

sources.title: Tutul Xiu
sources.note: Xiu rule at Mayapan c.1180-1280, expelled c.1400, revolt 1441, ambassadors to Montejo the Younger c.1539, mission at Mani 1547, Mani Land Treaty 1557; no extent given.

notes: NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no row for this province; Later Mayan City-States (1429-1546, 135,136 to 187,745 km2) covers the whole northern lowlands and contains it. The Kuchkabal page says the extent of the provinces 'is still debated' and that scholars disagree 'on whether they were territorial units or jurisdictions'; the shape here is a disc around the capital, soft, and no frontier is claimed. Cliopatria keeps its envelope to 1546 although the Spanish took the provinces one by one from 1527. TUTUL XIU. Start 1441 is the revolt, the page's infobox says 'after 1461'. End 1547 is the mission; the Xiu were already allied (about 1539). The Mani Land Treaty of 1557 'resolved a border dispute between the Xiu of Mani, the Cocom of Sotuta and the Copul [sic, Cupul]' but gives no line. Gazetteer lacks 'Maní'.
